 He was the first to call: Sarfaraz recalls Gambhir's support in dressing room leak row
 Sarfaraz Khan has revealed how Gautam Gambhir stood by him after allegations of leaking dressing-room information following the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. Gambhir called him twice, advised him to stay away from politics and also reassured his father during the difficult period.
 Advertisement Sarfaraz Khan recalls how Gautam Gambhir stood by him after dressing-room leak row. Courtesy: PTI By: India Today Sports Desk New Delhi , Nov 20, 2026 23:11 IST Last Updated Nov 20, 2026 23:11 IST Published by sabyasachi chowdhury Nov 20, 2026 23:11 IST Written By Sabyasachi Chowdhury Sarfaraz Khan has opened up about a difficult period following India's 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy campaign, revealing how head coach Gautam Gambhir reached out to him after allegations that he had leaked dressing-room information. The Mumbai batter said the controversy left him under considerable stress, but Gambhir personally called him and advised him to stay away from unnecessary politics and concentrate on cricket.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Gambhir also spoke to Sarfaraz's father, Naushad Khan, and reassured his family as the allegations began taking a toll on them. Recalling the episode in an interview with Aakash Chopra, Sarfaraz said he was particularly worried about how his parents and wife were coping with the situation.
 "I had to switch off my phone. GG sir (Gautam Gambhir) called me twice. He told me that these are useless talks and not to get involved in this politics and focus on your game. I told him that I can understand it, but my father is sad, and even my wife has been crying,” Sarfaraz said.
 “GG sir spoke to my father and told him to stop giving importance to such talks and let Sarfaraz play cricket, as he is a good cricketer. He told my father to call him if he needs any help. He was the first one to call me,” Sarfaraz added. SARFARAZ RECALLS THE STRESSFUL PERIOD
 The controversy emerged against the backdrop of tensions in the Indian dressing room during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. Reports about Gambhir expressing his displeasure with the team's performances after the Melbourne Test had triggered widespread discussion about the atmosphere within the squad. Reports stated that Gambhir had delivered stern remarks to the players after India lost the fourth Test. 
 Sarfaraz, who was part of India's squad for the series but did not feature in any of the five Tests, said he was hurt by the allegations when he returned home. He also recalled how the speculation caught him off guard while he was recovering from an injury.
 "I was hurt. The moment my flight landed, I started getting calls and messages. A lot was written on social media. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy had ended 20-25 days ago. I was hit during the BGT, and I went to NCA for rehab. Suddenly, the news of dressing room leak allegations started circulating. I was wondering whom I should speak to," he said. 'NOTHING OF THIS SORT HAPPENED'
 Sarfaraz firmly denied leaking any information from the dressing room and questioned why he would have continued to receive selection opportunities if the allegations were true. He also spoke about the impact the episode had on his family and the difficulty of dealing with speculation on social media.
 advertisement "Whom should I tell? Nothing of this sort happened, and if it were the case, I would not have been selected for the India A team and then for the Sri Lanka series. I don't know who said this. I was feeling bad, and if I was calling someone, my call was not answered. I was a bad time for my family.
 “My life is full of struggle, and I was ready to face it. I feel bad for my father, mother, wife and brother. Even a small thing turns big on social media. I heard a saying long ago. If you can't spoil someone's work, spoil their name. The work will get spoiled automatically," he added.
 Sarfaraz has played six Tests for India, scoring 371 runs at an average of 37.10, including one century and three half-centuries. His last international appearance came against New Zealand at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai in November 2024.
 He was subsequently part of India's squad for the Australia tour but did not play a Test. He was also called up as an injury replacement of Sai Saudharhan for the 2026 Sri Lanka Test series but did not make the playing XI in either match. - Ends Must Watch
